clue.text: It enables one to cross without being seen

definitions.text: It enables one to cross without being seen

parts.words: It enables one to cross without being seen
parts.note: surface reading: something that lets a person get across a road or border unobserved, like a smuggler's route
setter's reading: to cross is to mark an X on a voting paper, done in private

explanation.surface: A spy describes a hidden route for slipping over a frontier unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like a verb of travel; it means marking a cross on a voting slip, which in a SECRET BALLOT nobody else gets to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A vote cast privately lets each elector mark their choice on paper away from anybody's gaze.

clue.text: Bacon's lines may be so described

definitions.text: Bacon's lines may be so described

parts.note: surface reading: verses or sentences written by Francis Bacon, the Elizabethan essayist
setter's reading: the lines are the bands of fat and lean in a rasher of bacon

explanation.surface: A literary critic characterises the writing style of the philosopher Francis Bacon.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B suggests the writer; the lines are really the stripes of fat through a rasher. STREAKY bacon is the British name for what Americans call ordinary bacon strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Rashers cut from the belly carry alternating stripes of fat and meat, so they are marked with streaks.

clue.text: Mouse catcher not yet used in the plant

parts.note: a cat is the classic hunter of mice
in mint condition means new and unused

explanation.surface: A cat that has not yet chased a mouse lies hidden among the garden plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, cats love this plant, also called catnip.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint is a herb of the nettle family whose scent famously excites domestic felines.

clue.text: Happy-go-lucky midshipman goes on leave

indicators.note: one part goes on, meaning it is followed by, the next part

parts.note: Mr Midshipman Easy is the hero of Captain Marryat's naval novel
going, as a noun, is leaving or departure

explanation.surface: A cheerful young naval officer heads off on shore leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The midshipman is the title character of Marryat's 1836 novel Mr Midshipman Easy, a common crossword reference.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a relaxed, carefree temperament that does not worry about what happens next.

clue.text: Device that's defective, for example, is rejected

parts.note: faulty, not working properly

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so these letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the usual abbreviation, Latin exempli gratia

explanation.surface: A faulty gadget gets turned down as an example of poor workmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Device' sounds like a machine, but here it is the heraldic sense: an emblem or insignia.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry a device is an emblem or symbol, the kind of thing worn as a badge.

clue.text: Involved in a cult that's crazy

indicators.note: something involved is tangled up, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a cult is thought to have lost their mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, lunatic means wildly foolish or mad, so it can replace crazy.

clue.text: Not at home with shy, rejected person

parts.note: if you are out you are not in
to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A shy, shunned individual is never at home to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' reads as timid, but it is the verb meaning to fling.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is somebody driven out or shunned by society, an individual cast aside.

clue.text: Innocent chap in trouble driven to take away furniture

definitions.note: a description of a vehicle; read it as 'thing driven to take away furniture'

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests things in disarray, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blameless man in a fix is forced to haul away his furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: A PANTECHNICON is the British name for a large furniture removal van.
explanation.definitionFit: This large lorry is used by removal firms to carry household goods from one home to another.

clue.text: Charges put region back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the wrong way, so the combined letters are read from the end

parts.note: to set something is to put it down
a district or zone

explanation.surface: An official returns charges owed to a particular district.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run of letters is read backwards, not just the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging a drink means filling it with gas, which is what a soda maker does when it aerates water.

clue.text: Needs to set points out

indicators.note: to set is to arrange, so the letters are put into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Somebody must lay out the dots or marks on a diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set points out' looks like one phrase; split it after 'set' to find the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To denote something is to indicate or signify it, much as one would show or mark it.

clue.text: A challenging demand

parts.note: surface reading: a request that is hard to fulfil
setter's reading: issuing a challenge to a duel, in which the insulted party demands redress for their honour

explanation.surface: A boss makes a request that will be tough to meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Challenging' means difficult on the surface; it is really the gentleman's challenge to a duel, where one would say 'I demand satisfaction'.
explanation.definitionFit: In duelling custom, the wronged party sought reparation for an insult, formally called satisfaction.

clue.text: Recording start of the sport of kings

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word
horse racing is traditionally called the sport of kings

explanation.surface: A commentator records the opening of a horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracing is copying or recording a line, as a pen on a seismograph traces a reading.

clue.text: Competitor, presumably not an outsider

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a participant in a race or contest

definitions.note: a playful description: someone who has gone in is no longer outside
definitions.meaning: second meaning: one who has gone in, so is inside rather than out

explanation.surface: A racing tipster backs a contender who is not expected to be a long shot.
explanation.walkthrough: An outsider is a long-odds runner; the joke is that anyone who has entered is no longer outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who signs up for a race or contest is a participant in it, one who has entered.

clue.text: Keen, exercising for vault

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: An eager athlete practises for the pole vault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' looks like the adjective meaning eager; it is the verb meaning to lament, and 'vault' is the noun, an underground chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground chamber beneath a church, often with an arched stone roof.

clue.text: Acts die in variety shows

indicators.note: variety implies diversity, so the letters come out in a different form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Performers flop on stage at variety shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variety shows' reads as music-hall entertainment; 'variety' signals the rearrangement and 'shows' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs mean to point to or make something evident, so one can stand for the other.

clue.text: Pack freight in view on board

definitions.note: describes the goods; read as 'goods in view on board'

parts.note: a pack of playing cards is a deck
goods carried by a ship

explanation.surface: A docker loads goods onto a ship where they can be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: Most freight goes below in the hold; this kind is stowed on the open deck, where it can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods stowed on the open upper surface of a vessel rather than below in the hold are visible from shipboard.

clue.text: Upset at closing, remembering happier times?

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over, so the letters fall into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone saddened at the closing of a beloved place thinks back to better days.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for the past, so a nostalgic person looks back fondly on earlier years.

clue.text: Obvious way to get round the foreigner

indicators.note: to get round something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
an alien is a person from another country

explanation.surface: An outsider finds the clearest route around an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient point is the one that stands out most, prominent and noticeable to anybody.

clue.text: Messenger has a job getting in beer

indicators.note: getting in means going inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a type of beer
a post is a position of employment

explanation.surface: A courier lands work fetching in the beer supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Greek apostolos means one sent out, hence a messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Greek for one sent forth, and the apostles were sent to spread the Christian message.

clue.text: Mother is surrounded by sailors taking turn for a dance

indicators.note: taking a turn means facing about, so the letters run the other way
being surrounded means enclosed, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ABs are able seamen
familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum is whisked around the floor by crewmen, each taking a turn to partner her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking turn for a dance' reads as queuing to partner someone; 'turn' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The samba is a lively Brazilian ballroom and carnival dance of African origin.

clue.text: Juries are wrong to admit being exhausted

definitions.note: the answer completes the phrase rather than replacing it: juries are sworn in

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece is taken inside another

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong
worn out, tired

explanation.surface: A judge complains that juries wrongly confess they are tired.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a sentence fragment: what happens to juries at the start of a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: Jurors take an oath before hearing a case, so jurors are formally sworn in by the court.

clue.text: He is sorry for one who is late

definitions.text: He is sorry for one who is late

parts.words: He is sorry for one who is late
parts.note: surface reading: someone apologising for or pitying a person who turned up behind time
setter's reading: the late means the dead, so this is somebody grieving

explanation.surface: A host feels pity for a guest who arrives behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means tardy on the surface but deceased underneath, as in 'the late king'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person grieving at a funeral feels sorrow for the deceased, the one described as late.

clue.text: Appeal — and how the umpire may react?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to shout for help or attention
second meaning: an umpire answering a cricket appeal raises a finger and declares the batsman dismissed

explanation.surface: A bowler appeals and waits to see whether the umpire agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the fielding side appeals ('Howzat?') and the umpire may give the batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: To shout for something is a plea, and an umpire upholding a cricket appeal announces the dismissal aloud.

clue.text: Meeting in the course of a country stroll

indicators.note: something in the course of a phrase lies partway along it, inside the words

parts.note: spans the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Two lovers meet secretly during a walk in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a romantic rendezvous, a prearranged private appointment between lovers.

clue.text: One may peg out playing it

definitions.text: One may peg out playing it

parts.words: One may peg out playing it
parts.note: surface reading: someone may die while playing a strenuous game
setter's reading: in this lawn game, a player finishes by striking the ball against the central peg

explanation.surface: A grim warning that a player might drop dead mid-game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peg out' is British slang for die, but it is also the term for hitting the final peg to finish a game of CROQUET.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawn game with mallets and hoops ends when a ball strikes the winning stake, called pegging out.

clue.text: A sign that visitors aren't welcome

definitions.text: A sign that visitors aren't welcome

parts.words: A sign that visitors aren't welcome
parts.note: surface reading: some hint or gesture that guests should leave
setter's reading: a literal notice board barring the way in

explanation.surface: A frosty host signals that guests should not linger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sign' reads as a hint or signal; it is a literal notice on a door or road.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice forbidding access tells people they may not go through the door or gate.

clue.text: Meet and collide

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to encounter someone by chance
second meaning: to crash into something

explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet and collide' looks like one event; it is two separate senses of the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers bumping into an acquaintance unexpectedly and physically crashing into an obstacle.

clue.text: Rest centre or new meeting place in town

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters are formed into a fresh word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A council debates building a rest centre or a fresh community hub downtown.
explanation.definitionFit: The spot where two roads join is a traditional place for people to gather and chat in a city.
